html:
The Great Plains are the broad, flat grasslands of North America that run east of the Rocky Mountains from the Canadian prairies south into Texas. They are dry, windy, hot in summer and cold in winter.

For thousands of years people hunted bison there on foot, while farming peoples such as the Mandan grew maize in the river valleys. In the 1700s horses, spread north from the Spanish colonies, changed everything. Peoples such as the Comanche, the Lakota and other Sioux and the Blackfoot moved onto the grasslands and built a mounted bison-hunting life.

The United States took the plains in the later 1800s. Railways crossed them, hunters carried out the bison slaughter, and wars forced the Native nations onto reservations. Homesteaders broke the sod, and wheat such as Turkey Red made the region a breadbasket. Ploughing and drought brought the Dust Bowl of the 1930s. Since the 1950s center-pivot irrigation has watered fields from deep groundwater, which is now running down.
sum: The Great Plains are the broad, flat grasslands of North America that run east of the Rocky Mountains from the Canadian prairies south into Texas. They are dry, windy, hot in summer and cold in winter.
